title: Relative zigzag categories and two-sided homotopy calculus of fractions
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a category [def-nagata-category] and $W\subseteq\mathcal C$ a subcategory containing all objects and all identity maps. Enlarge universes so all categories below are small. A word is a finite list of letters $+$, $+_W$, $-$, read from the source on the left to the target on the right. Define $Z_w(x,y)$ as the category of diagrams with endpoints $x,y$, one horizontal arrow for each letter, directed right for $+$ and $+_W$ and left for $-$. Arrows at $-$ and $+_W$ lie in $W$; arrows at $+$ are unrestricted. Morphisms are commuting diagrams with all vertical arrows in $W$ and identities at the endpoints. Composition is vertical composition. Write $NZ_w(x,y)$ for its ordinary nerve, the simplicial set [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set] of composable strings of morphisms, with faces composing or deleting arrows and degeneracies inserting identities. A weak homotopy equivalence of simplicial sets means a map whose geometric realization induces a bijection on path components and isomorphisms on every homotopy group at every basepoint. The pair $(\mathcal C,W)$ admits a two-sided homotopy calculus of fractions if, for every $x,y$ and integers $r,s>0$, the identity-insertion functors induce weak homotopy equivalences
$$NZ_{-+^{r+s}-}(x,y)\longrightarrow NZ_{-+^r-+^s-}(x,y),\qquad NZ_{-(+_W)^{r+s}-}(x,y)\longrightarrow NZ_{-(+_W)^r-(+_W)^s-}(x,y).$$
In each insertion the vertex separating the two forward blocks is repeated and the new leftward arrow is its identity; a block of length zero contributes no arrow. In particular $Z_{-+-}(x,y)$ is the category of unrestricted three-arrow zigzags $x\leftarrow u\to v\leftarrow y$ with outer arrows in $W$, and morphisms as above.
